<reason>Side B (PRO) built the stronger path to victory by effectively neutralizing Side A's extreme cases with the "when possible" qualifier, reframing A's caregiver burden argument as a critique of underfunded status quo rather than supported home care, and delivering a closing that weaponized A's "early facility placement" admission to portray the CON position as advocating premature institutionalization. While A made a sophisticated argument about default incentives and the impossibility of scheduled safety, B successfully countered with evidence of institutional failures (understaffing ratios, infection risks) and preserved the autonomy stakes, leaving the PRO side with the cleaner comparative case on the proposition as written.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side B's Rebuttal 2 answers (A1/A2) decisively dismantled Side A's pressure questions by clarifying that routine clinical assessments manage transitions and that most seniors require only intermittent support, making A's 24/7 staffing cost argument a strawman; this, combined with B's closing capture of A's "early facility placement" language, exposed the CON position as structurally requiring premature institutionalization of capable seniors.</best_rebuttal>
